# wallix-bastion_connection_policy (Data Source)

Get information on a connection policy.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Get information about a specific connection policy
data "wallix-bastion_connection_policy" "ssh_policy" {
  connection_policy_name = "SSH"
}

# Reference the connection policy when configuring a device service
resource "wallix-bastion_device_service" "ssh_service" {
  device_id         = wallix-bastion_device.server1.id
  service_name      = "SSH"
  protocol          = data.wallix-bastion_connection_policy.ssh_policy.protocol
  connection_policy = data.wallix-bastion_connection_policy.ssh_policy.connection_policy_name
  port              = 22
}

# Inspect the policy's protocol and allowed authentication methods
output "ssh_policy_info" {
  value = {
    protocol               = data.wallix-bastion_connection_policy.ssh_policy.protocol
    type                   = data.wallix-bastion_connection_policy.ssh_policy.type
    authentication_methods = data.wallix-bastion_connection_policy.ssh_policy.authentication_methods
    options                = jsondecode(data.wallix-bastion_connection_policy.ssh_policy.options)
  }
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connection_policy_name` (String)

### Read-Only

- `authentication_methods` (Set of String)
- `description` (String)
- `id` (String) The ID of this resource.
- `options` (String, Sensitive)
- `protocol` (String)
- `type` (String)

## Usage Notes

### Lookup Key

- **connection_policy_name**: The name of the connection policy to look up. Returns an error if no policy with this name exists.

### Returned Attributes

- **protocol**: The underlying protocol (e.g. `SSH`, `RDP`, `RAWTCPIP`, `TELNET`, `RLOGIN`, `VNC`, `WEBAPP`)
- **type**: The specific policy variant (e.g. `RDP-JUMPHOST`). If the API does not return a distinct type, this falls back to the same value as `protocol`.
- **description**: Description of the policy
- **authentication_methods**: Set of authentication methods allowed for this policy (e.g. `PASSWORD_VAULT`, `PUBKEY_VAULT`, `KERBEROS_FORWARDING`, depending on protocol)
- **options**: The protocol-specific options as a JSON-encoded string; use `jsondecode()` to work with it as a Terraform object

### Working with `options`

Since `options` is returned as a raw JSON string, decode it before reading nested values:

```terraform
locals {
  ssh_options = jsondecode(data.wallix-bastion_connection_policy.ssh_policy.options)
}
```
